text: The MFA exception for three legacy service accounts is a real risk, written down on purpose. This lesson plans the compensating control: zero-trust micro-segmentation that contains them even if MFA never covers them.
The pilot starts with a default-deny network baseline. Every legacy service account gets exactly one explicit allow rule, to one destination -- nothing else is reachable.
svc-core-banking-sync, specifically, is planned to reach only the core-banking sync service's own private endpoint. Nothing else on Oakmere's network sits in its path.
This doesn't stop a stolen credential from working at that one endpoint. It stops that credential from going anywhere else -- which is the actual promise zero-trust segmentation makes.
Next: architecting the Python automation that watches sign-ins through a completely different lens than Sentinel's own rules.
